episodes.label: The Red Ink That Left a Shadow — Synchrotron XRF/XRD Mapping of Tebtunis Temple Papyri, Hematite Strokes With Lead-Phosphate Coffee-Ring Halos & Roman Bronze Inkwell Corrosion
episodes.notes: Synchrotron archaeometry of ancient Egyptian medical/ritual papyri (#39): Christiansen et al.'s (2020 PNAS) sub-micrometer XRF/XRD/FTIR mapping of 12 Tebtunis temple-library fragments showing hematite red-ocher pigment surrounded by sub-visible lead-phosphate/sulfate coffee-ring margins and lead palmitate, copper-bearing soot in Pathyris/Tebtunis black inks (2017), and Sibilia et al.'s (2021) Este Roman bronze inkwell distinguishing carbon-gum ink from container-corrosion cerussite (84% of Pb) and malachite.

episodes.label: Three Millennia of Medical Ink: Clay, Papyrus, Silk & Amate on Trial
episodes.notes: Comparative philological audit of three millennia of global medical literature. Traces the evolution of healing texts from Esagil-kin-apli's clay tablets and Egyptian papyri to Greco-Roman codices, Islamic translation workshops, and Nahuatl manuscripts.

episodes.label: Baked Clay & Sacred Reed: Sakikkū Tablets & Twelve Egyptian Papyri
episodes.notes: Archaeological and physiological audit of Bronze Age Mesopotamian cuneiform diagnostics within Esagil-kin-apli's forty Sakikkū tablets and twelve surviving Egyptian medical papyri. Evaluates clinical prognosis models, herbal pharmacology, and nosological categorization across Nippur texts and the Edwin Smith and Ebers papyri.

episodes.label: Sixty Scrolls on Cos & Alexandrian Vivisection: Hippocrates to Herophilus
episodes.notes: Archaeometric and historical audit of the Hippocratic Corpus and the brief 30-year window of human vivisection in Ptolemaic Alexandria under Herophilus and Erasistratus. Analyzes the mortality ledgers of Epidemics I and III alongside the transition from humoral theory to the anatomical investigations that defined early Greek and Alexandrian medicine.

episodes.label: Fire in the Temple of Peace: Celsus, Galen & Byzantine Surgery
episodes.notes: Philological and surgical reconstruction of the Greco-Roman medical corpus following the 192 CE Temple of Peace fire. Analyzes the preservation of Celsian operative techniques and Galenic anatomical treatises through the Byzantine encyclopedic traditions of Oribasius and Paul of Aegina, incorporating the 2005 discovery of the Peri Alypias codex.

episodes.label: Silk Tombs, Birch-Bark Scrolls & Tibetan Thangkas: Asian Medical Canons
episodes.notes: Philological and paleopathological survey of classical Asian medical canons. Examines excavated Mawangdui silk manuscripts, the Huangdi Neijing, Zhang Zhongjing's Shanghan Lun, Sushruta Samhita, and the Tibetan Four Tantras.

episodes.label: Twin Arks of Medical Memory: Baghdad House of Wisdom & Nahuatl Codices
episodes.notes: Comparative historiographic analysis of medical knowledge preservation in the Abbasid Translation Movement and the post-conquest Nahuatl codices. Synthesizes the Arabic rescue of Galenic anatomy by Hunayn ibn Ishaq with the botanical taxonomies of the 1552 Badianus Manuscript to trace the survival of global pharmacological traditions.

episodes.notes: One-Ångström Giants five-act historical discovery, atomic PDB & comparative One-Medicine treatise: Utako Okamoto's 1962 Tranexamic Acid Discovery to CRASH-2 (20,211) & WOMAN (20,060) 3-Hour Survival Cliff, Plasminogen Kringle-1 Zwitterion Lock (PDB 1CEB) vs. Tenecteplase PAI-1 Shield (PDB 1TPK), Intrathecal GABA_A Status Epilepticus (PDB 6X3T) & Retired Racing Greyhound Hyperfibrinolysis.

episodes.notes: Five-act paleopathology, archaeogenomics & historical linguistics investigation: Broca's Yucay Skull, Inca Bevel-Scraping (80% Survival vs. 50% Civil-War Hospital Mortality) & Monro–Kellie Pressure Physics.

episodes.label: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
episodes.notes: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

episodes.label: The Toe That Had to Walk — Ancient Egyptian Wooden & Cartonnage Prosthetic Great Toes, TT95A Bioarchaeology & Gait Lab Biomechanics
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and biomechanical evaluation of the Cairo wooden toe (JE 100016a from TT95A) and British Museum Greville Chester cartonnage toe (EA29996): healed first-MTP amputation, refitting wear marks, and Finch et al. (2012) Salford gait-lab kinematics and plantar pressure mat experiments.

episodes.label: The Lens That Never Left the Eye — Ancient Cataract Couching in Celsus & Sushruta, α/γ-Crystallin Optics, Aphakic Refraction & Survey Outcomes
episodes.notes: From Celsus and Sushruta's descriptions of cataract couching to alpha/gamma-crystallin short-range order, zonular lysis, why a displaced lens restores light transmission while leaving the eye ~+10 D aphakic, and the 249-eye Nigerian survey separating presenting vs. pinhole-corrected visual acuity.

episodes.label: The Leaf That Came Out Whole — Chimpanzee Rough-Leaf Swallowing, Vernonia Pith, Rakus Wound Care & Neolithic Durrington Coprolites
episodes.notes: Comparative evidence ledger across animal self-medication and paleoparasitology: physical Oesophagostomum worm expulsion via folded Aspilia leaves at Mahale, bitter Vernonia amygdalina sesquiterpene lactones, orangutan Fibraurea wound application, and fecal sterol/aDNA authentication of Neolithic Durrington Walls coprolites.

episodes.label: The Glue, the Chew, and the Wound — Neolithic Syltholm Birch Pitch, Betulin Triterpenes, Ancient Oral Metagenomes & Epidermolysis Bullosa Trials
episodes.notes: From a 5,700-year-old chewed birch bark pitch at Syltholm (Denmark) yielding a complete human genome and oral microbiome to GC-MS betulin/lupeol biomarkers, in vitro agar disk diffusion limits, and the Phase III EASE clinical trial of standardized birch triterpenes in epidermolysis bullosa.

episodes.label: The Tooth That Kept the Tool Marks — Neanderthal Molar Grooves, Villabruna Caries Scraping, Mehrgarh Bow-Drills & Lonche Beeswax
episodes.notes: Scanning electron microscopy, micro-CT, and FTIR spectroscopy of prehistoric worked teeth: Neanderthal interproximal toothpick grooves, Upper Paleolithic Villabruna carious lesion scraping, Neolithic Mehrgarh flint bow-drilled molars, and the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling.

episodes.label: The Spine That Looked Too Dense — Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DXA) Projection Geometry, Aortic Calcification & Contrast Artifacts, Vertebral Exclusions & ISCD Positions
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H037 (DXA Bone Densitometry & Projection Artifacts): how two-energy X-ray attenuation integrates all mineral along the beam path, why an L1 vertebral compression fracture and abdominal aortic calcification produced a high anteroposterior lumbar reading (Gupta et al. 2021), iodinated contrast (+3.8 to -1.5 T-score) and vertebral cement exclusions (+7.7 to -2.6 T-score, White et al. 2025), person-level vs. vertebra-level osteophyte and fracture comparisons in 96 women (Paiva et al. 2002), and the 2023 ISCD Adult Official Positions.

episodes.label: The Tooth They Drilled — Neolithic Mehrgarh Flint Bow-Drills, Villabruna Bitumen & Lonche Beeswax Dental Fillings Under SEM & Synchrotron Micro-CT
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and analytical investigation of prehistoric dentistry: concentric flint drill striations in Neolithic Mehrgarh molars (Coppa et al. 2006), Upper Paleolithic Villabruna and Riparo Fredian cavities, and synchrotron FTIR/radiocarbon verification of the 6,500-year-old Lonche beeswax filling (Bernardini et al. 2012).

episodes.label: The Seasons Inside a Tooth — Neanderthal Enamel Retzius Lines, Oxygen Isotopes, Barium Nursing Traces & Lead Bands
episodes.notes: High-resolution laser-ablation and SHRIMP microprobe reading of Neanderthal teeth (Smith et al. 2018): daily enamel cross-striations, seasonal oxygen-18 cycles, barium/calcium nursing transitions, and acute wintertime lead exposure bands.

episodes.label: The Opening That Stayed Open — Copper Age Pontecagnano Cranial Trepanation, Beveled Scraping Remodeling, Femoral Osteomyelitis & Modern CT Margins of Healed Skull Defects
episodes.notes: Osteological and radiological investigation of the 5,000-year-old Copper Age trepanned skull from Pontecagnano, southern Italy (Petrone et al.): broad watch-face outer scraping tapering to a lentil-sized inner aperture, obliterated diploic pores and smooth remodeled margins proving extended survival, severe femoral osteomyelitis in the same individual, and modern surgical CT correlates.

episodes.label: The Medicine We Cannot See — El Sidrón Neanderthal Dental Calculus Pyrolysis-GC/MS & aDNA, Chamomile/Yarrow/Poplar/Penicillium vs. Dental Abscess & Experimental Calculus Entrapment
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and experimental critique of prehistoric non-nutritive plant ingestion: El Sidrón Neanderthal dental calculus pyrolysis-GC/MS and shotgun metagenomics alongside a mandibular dental abscess and Enterocytozoon bieneusi infection (Hardy et al. 2012; Weyrich et al. 2017), experimental herbal mouth-rinse calculus entrapment models, and the evidentiary boundary between dietary/craft/environmental exposure and intentional self-medication.

episodes.label: What the Ice Kept in the Skin — Ötzi the Iceman's 61 Soot Tattoos, Multispectral Reflectance, Pazyryk Mummies & Therapeutic vs. Symbolic Puncturing
episodes.notes: Non-invasive multispectral photographic mapping and histological analysis of preserved ancient skin tattoos in glacial and permafrost mummies (Samadelli et al. 2015 on Ötzi's 61 tattoos across 19 anatomical groups), Raman carbon-soot chemistry, and testing the joint-degeneration acupuncture hypothesis.

episodes.label: The Foot That Healed — 31,000-Year-Old Borneo Distal Lower-Leg Amputation, Cortical Remodeling & Pleistocene Surgical Care
episodes.notes: Osteoarchaeological and paleopathological analysis of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo burial in Borneo (Maloney et al. 2022): healed distal tibia and fibula amputation with 6–9 years of post-operative survival and absence of osteomyelitis.

episodes.label: The Last Meal in the Bog — Tollund Man's Gut Contents, Barley-Flax-Weed Gruel, Whipworm Eggs & Forensic Reconstruction
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy forensic re-analysis of Tollund Man's large-intestinal contents (Nielsen et al. 2021): plant macrofossils, pollen, non-pollen palynomorphs, ancient DNA, proteins, lipids, Trichuris trichiura eggs, and why threshing waste was intentionally added.

episodes.label: 31,000 Years Before Anesthesia: Borneo Cave Amputation & Pleistocene Care
episodes.notes: Archaeopathological and bioarchaeological investigation of the 31,000-year-old Liang Tebo tibial-fibular surgical amputation in Borneo. Synthesizes prehistoric paleosurgery evidence with Shanidar 1 skeletal trauma, Pleistocene care dynamics, and ancestral plant-derived zoopharmacognosy.

episodes.label: Honey, Copper & Tetanus Inside the Edwin Smith & Ebers Papyri
episodes.notes: Quantitative wound-microbiology and orthopedic audit of the Edwin Smith and Ebers Papyri regarding hyperosmolar methylglyoxal honey and malachite copper ions. Analyzes the clinical management of Case 7 lockjaw and TMJ trauma alongside the biochemical risks of Clostridium tetani contamination in ancient Egyptian pharmacology.

episodes.label: Forehead Flaps, Ant-Jaw Staples & Couching Needles: Sushruta's Surgery
episodes.notes: Archaeometric and biomechanical investigation of the Suśruta Saṃhitā’s surgical protocols, focusing on supratrochlear artery pedicled forehead flaps and weaver-ant mandible intestinal staples. Reconstructs the clinical efficacy of ancient cataract couching and Dhoopana smoke antisepsis within the Varanasi medical lineage of 600 BCE.

episodes.label: Why Cortés Fired His Spanish Surgeons: Aztec Obsidian, Agave & Bone Nails
episodes.notes: Archaeological and clinical reconstruction of Mexica trauma care, comparing 3-nanometer Pachuca obsidian scalpels with European barber-surgeons. Examines hyperosmolar agave saponin wound sap and intramedullary pine bone pegs documented in the Florentine Codex.

episodes.label: Do Not Boil the Wormwood: Ge Hong's 340 CE Malaria Cure & Artemisinin
episodes.notes: Archaeometric and biochemical reconstruction of Ge Hong’s 340 CE cold-water extraction of Artemisia annua, which preserved the heat-labile endoperoxide bridge of artemisinin. Reconciles ancient pharmacological protocols with Tu Youyou’s modern rediscovery, contrasting hemozoin capping in quinine with the thermodynamic stability of modern ACT therapies.

episodes.label: Sacred Bark, Blowgun Curare & Sleeping Sponges to Modern Anesthesia
episodes.notes: Pharmacological and archaeomedical reconstruction of the lineage from ancient botanical toxins to modern balanced anesthesia. Traces the receptor-level transition from Amazonian curare-induced neuromuscular blockade and medieval spongia somnifera to the refined application of sodium-channel blockers and alkaloids in contemporary surgical practice.

episodes.label: Holes in the Living Skull: Why Inca Surgeons Beat Civil War Hospitals
episodes.notes: Bioarchaeological and historical evaluation of pre-Columbian Andean trepanation practices across Paracas and Inca Cuzco sites. Contrasts surgical survival statistics and sterile technique efficacy against nineteenth-century American Civil War cranial wound outcomes and septic mortality rates.

episodes.label: The Four-Humor Trap: Why Bloodletting Survived 2,000 Years & Flash Edema
episodes.notes: Physiological audit of ancient humoral bloodletting during acute cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema. Unpacks baroreceptor reflex mechanisms and Frank-Starling preload reduction that paradoxically alleviated specific cardiopulmonary emergencies.

episodes.label: Boiling Oil, Mercury Tubs & Antimony Pills: Great Iatrogenic Disasters
episodes.notes: Comparative iatrogenic audit of Renaissance surgical failures, from Giovanni da Vigo’s boiling elderberry oil to the toxic sequelae of Paracelsian mercury fumigation wards. Evaluates the 1537 accidental trial of Ambroise Paré alongside the pharmacologic persistence of reusable antimony pills and misdiagnosed sterile neutrophilic ulcers.

episodes.label: Ragusa Quarantine, Variolation & Outsmarting Contagion Before Germ Theory
episodes.notes: Archaeometric and epidemiological investigation of pre-germ theory contagion control, from Thucydides’ observations of acquired immunity to Ragusa’s 1377 maritime quarantine. Evaluates the ERAP2 selection pressure during plague outbreaks alongside the 1721 Newgate Prison variolation trials and early oral rehydration logic.

episodes.notes: Ancient urban hydrology and geoarchaeology at Classic Maya Tikal (#32): Scarborough et al.'s (2012) reservoir excavation framework, Tankersley et al.'s (2020) discovery of imported volcanogenic clinoptilolite/mordenite zeolites and macrocrystalline quartz in Corriental sediments, Lentz et al.'s (2020) cinnabar-derived mercury and Planktothrix cyanobacterial eDNA in central palace reservoirs, and 2021 arboreal sediment eDNA.

episodes.label: How Ancient Viruses Built Human Biology
episodes.notes: Molecular paleopathological investigation of endogenous retroviruses and their symbiotic role in the evolution of the mammalian placenta via syncytin expression. Synthesizes shotgun metagenomics with historical philology to reconstruct the ancient pathocenosis and genomic integration that fundamentally structured human biological systems.

episodes.label: How Disease Rewired Human History
episodes.notes: Paleopathological and sociopolitical investigation of the Antonine Plague, the Black Death, and the Justinian pandemics as catalytic engines of historical revolution. Examines how mass mortality events rewired economic structures and triggered institutional shifts, transforming the trajectory of civilizations through biological pressure.

episodes.label: How Math Stopped Pandemics
episodes.notes: Epistemological and statistical audit of the transition from miasmatic theory to spatial epidemiology during the 19th-century cholera outbreaks. Traces the development of early epidemiological differential equations and John Snow’s cartographic tracing methods that established the mathematical foundations for modern pandemic suppression.

episodes.label: How Humanity Explained Disease Before Microbes
episodes.notes: Historical and clinical audit of pre-microbial disease ontologies, ranging from miasma theory and humoral imbalances to divine retribution. Integrates modern veterinary diagnostics, such as fructosamine monitoring in hyperthyroid felines, to illustrate how metabolic shifts were misinterpreted before the advent of germ theory.

episodes.label: Dismantling the Public Health Shield
episodes.notes: Historical and paleopathological investigation of the catastrophic consequences following the erosion of civic sanitation and quarantine infrastructure. Analyzes the structural failure of public health shields across various epochs, demonstrating how the neglect of municipal hygiene and medical defenses precipitates the resurgence of endemic pathogens.

episodes.label: Ancient Parasites and Modern Health Politics
episodes.notes: Paleopathological and economic investigation of how parasitic infections like hookworm and malaria shaped colonial history and global health policy. Explores the evolutionary legacy of the Neolithic transition, where adaptation to ancient pathogens inadvertently increased the modern propensity for non-communicable autoimmune disorders.

episodes.label: Why We Blame Sickness On Sin
episodes.notes: Paleopathological and historical investigation of the persistent psychological bias linking disease etiology with moral failure across Babylonian, Biblical, and medieval eras. Examines how shifting epistemological frameworks shaped public health responses and social stigma.

episodes.label: Why Miners Pour Battery Acid on Parasites
episodes.notes: Ethnomedical and historical analysis of toxic folk remedies and occupational health hazards in 19th-century mining camps. Examines the desperate application of corrosive substances like battery acid to treat parasitic infections, reflecting the brutal intersection of industrial labor, medical scarcity, and the evolution of public health.

episodes.notes: Biomolecular archaeology and microbial ecology of Bronze Age fermented dairy from the Tarim Basin: LC-MS/MS proteomics of Xiaohe tomb dairy lumps (Yang et al. 2014), dental calculus milk peptides in seven Xiaohe individuals despite lactase non-persistence genotypes (Zhang et al. 2021), ancient DNA capture and phylogeny of 3,500-year-old Lactobacillus kefiranofaciens strains (Liu et al. 2024), and experimental metabolic cross-feeding in modern kefir communities (Blasche et al. 2021).

episodes.notes: Multi-proxy archaeological forensics at Durrington Walls (~2500 BCE): resolving the pig-bone vs. cattle/dairy potsherd lipid paradox through culinary segregation (Craig et al. 2015), five-isotope British livestock provenance (Madgwick et al. 2019), and Mitchell's coprolite paleoparasitology showing poorly cooked bovine/canid-shared tapeworm and capillariid infections.

episodes.label: What Pathogen DNA Can Date — Ancient Treponemal Genomes, Radiocarbon Calibration & Molecular Clock Boundaries
episodes.notes: Paleogenomic investigation of pre-Columbian Treponema pallidum and ancient pathogens (Majander et al. 2024; Barquera et al. 2025; 5,500-year-old Sabana de Bogota genome): damage patterns, radiocarbon priors, recombination filtration, and tip-dating limits.

episodes.label: What the Roman Drain Kept — Roman Latrine Archaeoparasitology, Helminth Eggs, Giardia ELISA & Coprolite Bile-Acid GC-MS
episodes.notes: Multi-proxy archaeoparasitological and biomolecular analysis of Roman sewer and latrine sediments: Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, Taenia spp., and Diphyllobothrium latum microscopy, Giardia duodenalis and Entamoeba histolytica antigen ELISA, and fecal sterol/bile-acid GC-MS.

episodes.label: How Untreated HIV Triggers Lymph Node Bystander Pyroptosis
episodes.notes: Immunopathological resolution of the "lymph node firetrap" driven by IFI16-mediated bystander pyroptosis in untreated HIV-1 infections. Examines the mechanistic transition from chronic viral replication to regulated cell death, illustrating how inflammatory crises and CD4+ T-cell depletion are orchestrated within the lymphatic microenvironment.

episodes.label: Influenza PANoptosis Versus Epstein Barr Cytokine Storms
episodes.notes: Mechanistic analysis of ZBP1-mediated PANoptosis during influenza infection and Epstein-Barr virus-driven hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Explores regulated cell death pathways and lethal cytokine storm immunopathology.

episodes.label: Parasitic Crystal Granulomas and the Steroid Worm Trap
episodes.notes: Pathological dissection of parasitic crystal granulomas and the "steroid worm trap" associated with Strongyloides hyperinfection. Analyzes the role of eosinophil EETosis and regulated cell death in the host-pathogen war, highlighting the lethal consequences of immunosuppression in the presence of dormant helminthic larvae within human tissue.

episodes.label: How Black Death Plague Shaped Modern Crohns Genetics
episodes.notes: Evolutionary and immunogenetic reconstruction of the selective pressure exerted by Yersinia pestis during the fourteenth-century Black Death. Analyzes the trade-off between YopJ-mediated pyroptosis resistance and the modern prevalence of Crohn’s disease associated with the ERAP2 locus, illustrating the lasting genomic legacy of the 1348 pandemic.

episodes.label: How Tuberculosis Liquefies Granulomas and Hijacks TNF
episodes.notes: Molecular reconstruction of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis "liquefied fortress" through the hijacking of TNF-alpha signaling and the induction of NAD+ depletion. Investigates the Goldilocks paradox of cytokine concentration in granuloma maintenance versus the necrotic collapse driven by the tuberculosis necrotizing toxin (TNT) pathway.
